pages.text: "No washing! Just sleep!" Bung clung to a post at the boat edge. The noodle boat stayed tied still. Hard, dry mud stuck to Bung's arms.
Boat lamps glowed one by one. Grandpa set a scoop by the big bucket. "I will sleep without washing, Grandpa!" Bung hid behind little Ddori.
But the arms itched. Dry mud flaked onto the floor. "Why so itchy?" Bung scratched hard.
Grandpa held up a full scoop. "Forget washing. Want a rain shower?" "A shower game?" Bung looked up.
Splash over Bung's shoulders! Mud streamed down to the calves. "Wow, a shower!" Bung laughed. Ddori laughed too.
"Shower games have steps." Grandpa unfolded his fingers. "Splash, rub with your hands, splash again. Pour a splash, shine clean!" Bung echoed.
Bung rubbed both arms, loosening the mud. Another splash from Grandpa! Dark arms grew smooth and clean. "Pour a splash, shine clean!"
Ddori's turn. Bung drew those little hands close, poured gently over their backs, and rubbed. Ddori stamped excitedly. "Ah! Ah!"
Bung spread three wet fingers. "One, splash! Two, rub! Three, splash again, shine clean!" Grandpa held a dry cloth and counted the fingers.
With the cloth, Grandpa patted Bung's back, then Ddori's. Now Bung knew how fresh washing felt. Grandpa chuckled. "Pour a splash, shine clean!"
